text:
The Avalanche just lost Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar at the same time, both with lower-body injuries, and then went into Montreal and won 4-1 anyway. The Associated Press called it a short-handed win, and that is the season for now: reports have MacKinnon out around a month and Makar for multiple weeks.

It hurts because of what they were. The MacKinnon line with Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas had outscored teams 20-10, and Makar with Devon Toews had taken 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) on the way to a 16-9 edge. Colorado is 12-6-3 with 27 points, has taken 53% of the five-on-five expected goals, and has points in five straight with 59% of the chances in that run. Our playoff odds were at 97% before anyone got hurt, and the cushion is real.

Now the depth carries it. Lehkonen moved to the top line and the top penalty kill and power play units in Montreal. Necas has been on a scoring run, Toews is producing again after a quiet year, and Nazem Kadri, Brock Nelson and Gabriel Landeskog give them a second line that wins its minutes.

The worry is in net. Scott Wedgewood is at .882 and 4.4 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Without the two stars, the goaltending has less room for error.
